items.title: Carl Rinker Interview, 1962-10-14
items.q: And uh you were in a succeeding band weren't you? Yes. Paley's band.

ctx.x: We used to come and play quite regular with us. It was called House of Niles. House of Niles. I think they played picnics out in through there and they would stop in for a beer afterwards and set in with the band. Oh yeah. I don't know how we could have earned eccentric any other way and we learned it. And uh I think I think Larry Shields taught us. I can't be sure. I think Leon Rapolo came uh came back to Chicago when I was playing with Ray Bozeman and uh played one night but it's been so long I can't remember.…

sure that I met him though. Uh Merez and uh Brunas for a long time held a job at Friars Inn, one of the best loop jobs in Chicago. And uh you were in a succeeding band weren't you? Yes. Paley's band. Bill Paley's band uh and you were the trumpet player along with uh uh Caffarelli was
